reason: The finding goes further than its data. What it measured holds: in-sample GT nuclei are ~30-130x depleted in the [0.94,0.965) band. Readmitted nodes stay depleted near GT after a density control (scratchpad node_class_ctrl.py: among nodes within 10 um of a GT node, readmitted 5.8% vs plain 34.6% in 44b6 and 16.2% vs 56.1% in 6bba, so 3.5-6x, not 7-8x). Gapfill peaks are 0/13 near GT. The step that fails is the claim that this is an 'in-sample artifact, VOID in both directions'. The same pattern follows from (b) annotation selection: annotators marked clearly visible nuclei, and any detector scores those high on unseen embryos too. It also follows from (c) a readmit next to a GT nucleus that a plain node has already claimed, which is a duplicate by construction. Only (a), memorisation, makes the lab unrepresentative, and no embryo-held-out test was run to tell (a) from (b) or (c). The text also overstates one point: 14.2%/17.2% of GT nodes have NO pool peak within 3 um, so it is not true that 'every annotated nucleus already has a >=0.965 peak'. Sub-threshold levers cannot reach those nuclei either. The out-of-sample reads are split or lean toward the old premise: frontier947+readmit 0.947 -> 0.946 on public; JT 0.958 -> 0.959; hikaggler/Ogurtsov found node-count calibration LB-predictive and saw no detector change move the LB (CONTEXT l.1071-1076); +3% nodes costs ~0.003 of the bonus. Memorisation can only bias the lab one way: ADD levers look worse, DROP levers look better. So the lab is one-sided, not void both ways, and the old R11-d3/R13NC-4 costs stay as the best available (optimistic) cost estimate for adding nodes. On feasibility it is harmless: documentation only, with no code, slot, runtime or R8 exposure. Pre-deadline value is 0, and no action depends on it before 29 Sep.
fix: Keep a softened lab caveat instead of VOID. Proposed wording: 'exp60 cannot sign sub-threshold node levers from the recall side. In-sample, 99.5% of GT nuclei that have a peak are >= 0.965, and readmits are 3.5-6x depleted near GT even after a density control. The cause is not identified (memorisation, annotation selection, or duplicates of already-claimed nuclei). If memorisation is the cause, the bias is one-sided: lab gains from DROPPING readmit/gapfill nodes are optimistic (treat like leaf prune, probe 27), and lab costs of ADDING them are an upper bound on harm.' Leave R11-d3/R13NC-4 standing as cost estimates with a pointer to this caveat, not as void. Leave R17-RC-A (b) as the leading hypothesis with reduced confidence, not demoted to 1-of-2. Correct the 'every annotated nucleus has a >=0.965 peak' wording (14-17% have none within 3 um). Post-deadline: settle (a) vs (b) on an embryo-held-out detector (6bba-only scratch on 44b6) before any node-recovery work. No pre-deadline change; R23-RC-A is judged on its own.
realistic_gain: 0 LB pre-deadline (documentation only; no slot, build or submission depends on it). Methodological only: it guards against lab-positive node-drop levers (already covered by the leaf-prune lesson) and orders post-deadline work. Measured leverage of the band is tiny anyway: at most +0.6% nodes at 0.94, with 14-17% of GT misses out of reach of any sub-threshold lever.
